payload.gap_claim:
INHERITS the first pass's scan and claim (evidence/frame_delta-1.json, superseded): three layers of code search with sequential escalation, offset/limit paging with refuse-and-redirect, and each alternative shedding either freshness or structure or history or auditability.

TWO CHANGES, and the first is a correction the rewalk forced.

1. THE CLAIM ABOUT OUR OWN POSITION WAS WRONG, and the correction comes from the owner rather than from the scan. The first pass argued that composing ripgrep and git was itself duplication - 'one question, two tools' - and used that to justify dropping ripgrep entirely. The owner's counter, in one line: THESE ARE TWO JOBS, NOT ONE. Searching a working tree and searching history are different questions with different answers, and using one tool for each is not duplication; it is fit. So the gap claim now reads: every alternative gives you either freshness or structure or history or auditability, and NONE gives all four - and the position that can is COMPOSITION, one tool per job, behind one lane that logs what was consulted. The first pass had the right composition and then talked itself out of half of it.

2. A SECOND GAP, which the first pass could not see: the field scan positions SEARCH TOOLS and says nothing about whether a gate's review actually happens. No agent tool surface we scanned makes the machine collect the review it demands of itself. That half is still unpositioned, and I would rather record it as unpositioned than claim novelty - but it is now the more valuable half, because it is the check that catches the first half going wrong.
payload.why_now:
INHERITS the first pass's four (the demand signal exceeded the cost of ignoring it; the dependency objection dissolved; the record moved out of the working tree at i5d; delegation became the default and exposed what it rests on).

A FIFTH, and it is the one that made the rewalk necessary rather than merely useful: THE DEFECT BECAME LEGIBLE. Three separate mechanisms were found written-but-never-collected within a few hours - the state-of-the-art scan, the applies_to guidance join, and the review rounds. One of those is an oversight. Three is a shape: v2's methods describe a process its evidence forms do not collect, so every method is advisory and the agent's diligence is the only thing enforcing any of it. That is knowable NOW in a way it was not this morning, and it is fixable at one place - the compiler that builds evidence forms.
payload.value_props:
PROP 1 (the agent walking the loop) and PROP 2 (the owner who owns an iteration they did not watch) are INHERITED unchanged, with needs N1-N9 and their pass lines.

ONE NEED IS CORRECTED and THREE ARE ADDED.

CORRECTED - N2, which the first pass satisfied on paper and violated in fact:
  need N2: find things without four attempts | outcome: ONE search answers WITH CONTEXT | PASS LINE, restated so it cannot be met by a design that returns locations only: a known line is located in ONE call AND the result carries the caller's requested surrounding lines. R3 says a match carries context; the first pass built locations-only and minted an ADR explaining why that was fine. The pass line now names the thing the requirement asks for, so no design can satisfy it by redefining it (se.law-requirements-are-never-weakened).

ADDED - PROP 2 gains three needs, because the owner's ability to trust a delegated gate is what the rewalk is about:
  need N10: a gate is reviewed, not just filled | outcome: every gate carries verify, validate, red-team and a verdict | PASS LINE: no gate can be submitted without all four, enforced by the form rather than by discipline - and a mechanical check asserts every gate in the machine carries them as REQUIRED.
  need N11: a reopen verdict does something | outcome: reopen re-activates the named states and their cone | PASS LINE: a reopen re-activates the cone, marks prior fills superseded, and LEAVES THE EVIDENCE READABLE - proven by reopening and then finding the first pass's claims still on disk.
  need N12: the red-team round is adversarial, not decorative | outcome: it names a kill-criterion and reports what looking for it found | PASS LINE: every redteam_round names the criterion that would make the decision wrong. Weaker than the others by nature - it constrains form, not sincerity - and recorded as such rather than overstated (se.raid-mandatory-rounds-degrade-into-ceremony).
payload.business_case:
SKIPPED, reason unchanged from the first pass: no acquirer, no revenue to model; quackitect is the owner's instrument. The currency stays the measured one - workarounds, re-derivations of existing rulings, and owner rounds per gate.

ONE FIGURE THE REWALK ADDS: this iteration's first pass cost the owner FOUR corrections that a review round would have caught before it reached them - the C5 misweighting, the R3 violation, the missing rounds, and the unimplemented reopen. Three of the four were catchable by reading the register against the work, which is precisely what validate_round is. That is the return this iteration is buying, and it is measurable next iteration rather than assertable now.
